title: Sales determination backbone
memory_rule: Header defines the commercial frame. Item category defines what the item is allowed to do. Schedule line defines how quantity and supply behave. Logistics and pricing then consume master data plus those controls.

rules.title: Item category determination
rules.assessment_hook: If the item behaves wrongly, first prove which item category was determined and why.

rules.title: Schedule line category determination
rules.assessment_hook: The same sales item can become a different supply process when its schedule-line control changes.

rules.title: Requirements / planning control
rules.assessment_hook: MTO is not explained by an SD item category alone. Follow the requirement type into PP/MRP.

rules.title: Shipping point determination
rules.assessment_hook: A missing shipping point is usually a missing or inconsistent input, not a delivery transaction problem.

rules.title: Pricing procedure determination
rules.assessment_hook: Do not debug a missing condition before proving that the expected pricing procedure was selected.

rules.title: Third-party procurement trigger
rules.assessment_hook: TPO replaces your outbound delivery with a purchasing chain; the sales order remains the commercial anchor.

rules.title: Advanced intercompany relevance
rules.assessment_hook: Different company codes alone do not explain the whole process. Prove whether the scenario is classic or advanced intercompany and which orchestration documents must exist.
